title: Micron Opens Second AI Memory Packaging Plant in Taichung
source_used: Seoul Economic Daily (citing Taiwan's Economic Daily News and Commercial Times)
key_facts: Micron, the world's third-largest memory chipmaker, held the opening ceremony for its second Advanced Assembly and Test Taichung plant (AATT2) at the Central Taiwan Science Park on 15 Oct 2026.
Donghui Lu, chairman of Micron Taiwan, said the plant builds capacity for HBM and AI-driven demand.
Customer bookings for HBM production are fully taken through 2027, and HBM demand growth should outpace conventional DRAM through 2028.
Micron will open an advanced HBM packaging plant in Singapore in 2027.
Taiwan President Lai Ching-te said Micron's cumulative Taiwan investment tops 1.6 trillion Taiwan dollars.
Fab 11 in Taoyuan, due to start in 2028, will use extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography.
The Micron union won a strike vote on 7 Oct backing a demand for 15 percent of operating profit; it plans a rally near the Presidential Office on 19 Oct and further action if no agreement by 22 Oct.
quote_evidence: Micron held an opening ceremony for its second Advanced Assembly and Test Taichung plant (AATT2) at the Houli campus of the Central Taiwan Science Park on the 15th, according to Taiwan's Economic Daily News and Commercial Times on the 16th.

Customer bookings for the company's HBM production facilities are fully taken through 2027, the chairman said, adding that HBM demand growth is expected to outpace that of conventional DRAM through 2028.
The union, however, plans to hold a rally near the Presidential Office on the 19th as scheduled, and says it will take further action if no specific agreement is reached by the 22nd.
why_it_matters_hint: More AI-memory packaging capacity in Taiwan, with a union dispute over profit sharing still open.
notes: Event is 15 Oct 2026, before the window. Our 15 Oct 2026 edition (item 46) already carried The Edge Malaysia's report on Taiwan's president urging Micron and the union to negotiate at this opening. AI-translated from Korean.
